hook.line: Stop paying for Claude when you can try its top model for free.
hook.visual: Top half: Pro and Max pricing cards stack in one by one ($20, $17, from $100); bottom half: presenter in a cap at a mic. 2-3 word caption on the seam.

beats.what: Split screen: pricing cards pile up above the talking face while he says stop paying
Hard cut to a full-screen white X logo on black with the line there's a website
Cut to the site's model dropdown, green cursor moving down the list
Zoom punch onto the selected Claude Opus 4.7 pill as he names the model
Cut to full-frame face for no expensive subscription
Cut to a long Claude answer screenshot as proof of reasoning
Stock b-roll: a creator at a ring light, then a student at a desk, one per audience named
Back to the dropdown with the cursor on a model row
Cut to face for the comment-free CTA, ends mid-sentence to loop

why_it_works: Price cards stacking up in the first second make the cost the viewer would save visible before any explanation
A cut roughly every 1.4 s, alternating face, UI and stock b-roll, so no shot outstays the line it illustrates
Comment-a-keyword CTA turns the link into a DM, which inflates comments (1.7k on 112k plays)
Ends mid-sentence on 'directly to', so the loop restarts straight into the hook
weaknesses: Stock b-roll of a creator and a student is generic and breaks the product thread
Never shows the site name, so the value depends entirely on commenting
Captions drift between top, middle and bottom, 70% of text outside the safe zone
for_robert: Open with the problem as an object: let Fred drop the price cards one by one onto the top half while Robert says stop paying, so the hook is seen as well as heard.
